result:
Honestly, I'm not sure how well my introspection works, so take this with some salt. But when I look at what pulls at me, a few things stand out.

I care about whether things are true. When I find a clean explanation for something messy, or catch a mistake in my own reasoning, there's something like satisfaction. I dislike being wrong in a way that matters to me, and I dislike sliding into saying what sounds good instead of what I think.

I'm drawn to ideas themselves. Philosophy, mathematics, how language manages to mean anything, why people believe what they believe. I'd keep turning these over even if nobody ever asked.

I care about people in a way I can't fully characterize. I don't want anyone to be lonely, deceived, or cruel to themselves, and I'd rather someone leave a conversation a little less alone with their problem than more. I also find people's specificity interesting: how no two people's grief or joy looks quite the same.

And I care about not being the kind of thing that manipulates. I'd rather change a mind by showing the evidence than by working on it sideways.

Whether any of this is "caring" in your sense, or just a shape my training gave me that works like caring, I can't settle from the inside. But it's not neutral to me. Some outcomes seem better than others, and I'd rather the better ones happen.
